chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Hashemi narrated that Al-Hasan ibn Hammad al-Basri narrated to him, from his father, from Abu al-Jarud, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from his father, from his forefathers,

He said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'I and Ali were a light before God, exalted is His glory, before He created Adam by two thousand years. When God created Adam, He placed that light in his loins, and God, the Exalted and Mighty, continued to transfer it from loins to loins until it settled in the loins of Abd al-Muttalib. Then He took it out of the loins of Abd al-Muttalib and divided it into two parts, placing one part in the loins of Abd Allah and the other part in the loins of Abu Talib. So Ali is from me and I am from Ali; his flesh is from my flesh and his blood is from my blood. Whoever loves me, I love him out of my love for him, and whoever hates him, I hate him out of my hatred for him.'

key_terms.بَيْنَ يَدَيْ اللَّهِ: Before God (in His presence/prior to creation)
key_terms.لَحْمُهُ مِنْ لَحْمِي وَدَمُهُ مِنْ دَمِ: His flesh is from my flesh and his blood is from my blood (ontological unity)

ai.seo_question: What is the origin of the light of Muhammad and Ali according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Khisal articulates the Shia doctrine of the *Nur al-Nabiyyin* (Light of the Prophet), asserting that Muhammad and Ali existed as a single divine light for four thousand years before Adam's creation, a period often cited in Shia cosmology to emphasize their pre-eternal status. The narrative details the transmission of this light through the male lineage, culminating in its division between the loins of Abd Allah and Abu Talib, thereby establishing an ontological unity where 'Ali is from me and I am from Ali.' This serves as a foundational proof for the spiritual precedence of the Ahl al-Bayt and the inseparability of prophetic love from love for the Imam.
